title: An Email to a Host Family
description: Practise future arrangements, polite questions and the present perfect, then write an email to a host family.
instructions: Do the exercises in Part 1. Then write your text in Part 2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: I ___ my cousin in London before I come to you.
exercises.explanation: Use the present continuous for fixed plans and arrangements in the future: I am visiting my cousin.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the verb in brackets.
exercises.text: I have never ___ (be) to England before.
exercises.explanation: To talk about travel experience, use have been to: I have never been to England.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: Could you tell me what I should bring?
exercises.explanation: In an indirect question after "Could you tell me", use normal word order: what I should bring (not what should I bring).

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: If you will need anything from my country, just let me know.
answers: If you need anything from my country, just let me know.
exercises.explanation: Do not use "will" after "if" in a first conditional. Use the present simple: if you need.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: Do I ___ bring a towel, or will you give me one?
exercises.explanation: "Need to" + infinitive asks if something is necessary. "Must" and "should" are never followed by "to".

exercises.prompt: Complete with however, although, in addition or as a result.
exercises.text: I'm very excited about the trip. ___, I'm a bit nervous about speaking English all the time.
exercises.explanation: "However" starts a new sentence with a contrasting idea.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I study English since I was eight.
answers: I have studied English since I was eight.
I have been studying English since I was eight.
I've studied English since I was eight.
I've been studying English since I was eight.
exercises.explanation: With "since", use the present perfect (simple or continuous), not the present simple.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word SHOULD. Begin: "Do you think ..."
exercises.text: Is it a good idea for me to bring warm clothes?
answers: Do you think I should bring warm clothes?
exercises.explanation: To ask for advice, use "Should I ...?": Should I bring warm clothes?

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: I'm really looking forward to ___ you all.
exercises.explanation: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so use the -ing form: looking forward to meeting.

exercises.prompt: Write the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.explanation: After "your kind" we need a noun. The noun from "invite" is "invitation".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: Would you mind meeting me at the airport?
exercises.explanation: "Would you mind" is a polite request and is followed by the -ing form.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: I enjoy to cook traditional dishes from my country.
answers: I enjoy cooking traditional dishes from my country.
exercises.explanation: "Enjoy" is followed by the -ing form, not the to-infinitive: enjoy cooking.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: My hometown is much ___ than London, so it will be a big change for me.
exercises.explanation: Short adjectives take -er in the comparative: small - smaller. "Much" makes it stronger.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word HAVE. Begin: "You ..."
exercises.text: It isn't necessary for you to meet me at the airport.
answers: You don't have to meet me at the airport.
exercises.explanation: "Don't have to" means something is not necessary.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with one word.
exercises.text: Could you ___ me up from the station when I arrive?
exercises.explanation: "Pick somebody up" means to collect them in a car.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: I'm sending a photo of my sister, ___ is coming to visit in August.
exercises.explanation: Use "who" for people. Between commas (extra information) we cannot use "that".

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: I used to have a dog.
exercises.explanation: Use "used to + infinitive" for a past situation that is no longer true.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: Cooking is one of the thing I like most.
answers: Cooking is one of the things I like most.
exercises.explanation: After "one of the" we use a plural noun: one of the things.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word ALTHOUGH. Begin: "Although ..."
exercises.text: My English isn't perfect, but I can understand most things.
answers: Although my English isn't perfect, I can understand most things.
exercises.explanation: "Although" shows a contrast. Do not use "but" in the same sentence.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word LIKE. Begin: "I would ..."
exercises.text: I want to visit Oxford during my stay.
answers: I would like to visit Oxford during my stay.
exercises.explanation: "Would like + to-infinitive" is a polite way of saying "want".

task.prompt: You are going to stay with a host family in England for three weeks this summer. Write an email to your host family to introduce yourself.
contentPoints: Say what you like doing in your free time.
Ask at least two questions about your stay.
task.modelAnswer:
Dear Mr and Mrs Taylor,

I'm writing to introduce myself before my stay with you in July. My name is Minh, and I'm sixteen years old. I live in Hanoi with my parents and my younger sister.

In my free time, I love playing badminton and taking photos. I also enjoy cooking, so I'd be happy to make a Vietnamese dinner for you one evening!

I'm arriving at Heathrow Airport on 5 July at 3 p.m. I've never been to England before, so I'm really excited. However, I'm a bit nervous about speaking English all the time.

Could you tell me what the weather is usually like in July? Should I bring warm clothes? Also, is there a bus from your house to the language school?

I'm really looking forward to meeting you.

Best wishes,
Minh
